title: I Built an Open-Weight AI That Prices Etsy Shops, On Your Laptop
why_read: A small practical project applying a lightweight tabular ML model to run entirely locally for small-business pricing decisions, interesting as an example of on-device ML for a concrete use case.
analysis: The author built a tool called PricePilot that predicts optimal pricing for Etsy shop listings using a model that runs entirely on the user's own laptop rather than a cloud service, using the TabPFN tabular prediction model. The motivation is a real small-business pain point around pricing physical products with many interacting factors like material, size, and season, and avoiding sending private sales data to third-party SaaS pricing tools. Using TabPFN, a relatively new foundation model designed specifically for small tabular datasets, is a mildly interesting technical choice worth knowing about even if the overall project is a modest hackathon submission. The privacy-and-cost framing is a reasonable practical argument for local inference even though the underlying ML technique isn't itself novel.
